\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تکذیب} \fa{کردن} (takzib kardan)}{تکذیب کردن (takzib kardan)}]{\fa{تکذیب} \fa{کردن} (takzib kardan) — to refute, to deny (a report)}

\label{lesson:FA-C310-takzib-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to announce, then the Persian for to state.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تکذیب} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تکذیب} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{takzib kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to refute, to deny (a report)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{وزیر} \fa{این} \fa{خبر} \fa{را} \fa{تکذیب} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Vazir in khabar râ takzib kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The minister denied this report.
\end{quote}

For denying a report or a rumour in public. Present \emph{takzib mikonad}. The opposite is \emph{ta'yid kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{takzib} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{takdhīb}, \textquotedblleft{}calling something a lie\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takzib kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takzib kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{takzib kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to announce, then the Persian for to state, then say \emph{takzib kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{تکذیب} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To refute, to deny (a report)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تایید} \fa{کردن} (ta'yid kardan)}{تایید کردن (ta'yid kardan)}]{\fa{تایید} \fa{کردن} (ta'yid kardan) — to confirm, to approve}

\label{lesson:FA-C310-tayid-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to state, then the Persian for to refute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تایید} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تایید} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ta'yid kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to confirm, to approve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{خبر} \fa{را} \fa{تایید} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis khabar râ ta'yid kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police confirmed the report.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{ta'yid mikonad}. Careful print adds a hamza sign over the alef.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ta'yid} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ta'yīd}, \textquotedblleft{}support, backing\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ta'yid kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to state, then the Persian for to refute, then say \emph{ta'yid kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیگیری} \fa{کردن} (peygiri kardan)}{پیگیری کردن (peygiri kardan)}]{\fa{پیگیری} \fa{کردن} (peygiri kardan) — to follow up, to pursue}

\label{lesson:FA-C310-peygiri-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to refute, then the Persian for to confirm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیگیری} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پیگیری} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{peygiri kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to follow up, to pursue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خبرنگار} \fa{این} \fa{خبر} \fa{را} \fa{تا} \fa{آخر} \fa{پیگیری} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khabarnegâr in khabar râ tâ âkhar peygiri kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The journalist followed this story through to the end.
\end{quote}

\emph{pey} \textquotedblleft{}footstep, track\textquotedblright{} + \emph{giri} \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}: to keep following the trail of something. Present \emph{peygiri mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{peygiri} joins \emph{pey} \textquotedblleft{}footstep, track\textquotedblright{} and \emph{giri} \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}, both native Persian; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited too. EtymDB lists no entry for the compound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peygiri kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{peygiri kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to refute, then the Persian for to confirm, then say \emph{peygiri kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خبر} \fa{دادن} (khabar dâdan)}{خبر دادن (khabar dâdan)}]{\fa{خبر} \fa{دادن} (khabar dâdan) — to let someone know, to tell the news}

\label{lesson:FA-C310-khabar-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to confirm, then the Persian for to follow up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خبر} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{خبر} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{khabar dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to let someone know, to tell the news\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دوستم} \fa{به} \fa{من} \fa{خبر} \fa{داد} \fa{که} \fa{برادرش} \fa{ازدواج} \fa{کرده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dustam be man khabar dâd ke barâdarash ezdevâj karde ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My friend let me know that his brother had got married.
\end{quote}

The person told takes \emph{be}: \emph{be mâdaram khabar dâdam}. Present stem \emph{dah-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khabar} \textquotedblleft{}news\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{khabar} (EtymDB). \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian: to give the news.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khabar dâdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khabar dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khabar dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to confirm, then the Persian for to follow up, then say \emph{khabar dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اطلاع} \fa{دادن} (ettelâ' dâdan)}{اطلاع دادن (ettelâ' dâdan)}]{\fa{اطلاع} \fa{دادن} (ettelâ' dâdan) — to inform, to notify}

\label{lesson:FA-C310-ettela-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to follow up, then the Persian for to let someone know.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اطلاع} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{اطلاع} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{ettelâ' dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to inform, to notify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هتل} \fa{به} \fa{ما} \fa{اطلاع} \fa{داد} \fa{که} \fa{اتاق} \fa{آماده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hotel be mâ ettelâ' dâd ke otâq âmâde ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hotel informed us that the room was ready.
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{khabar dâdan}. Present \emph{ettelâ' midahad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ettelâ'} \textquotedblleft{}information\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{iṭṭilā'}; EtymDB lists the Persian word with no parent. \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
